title: Continue The Project And Adapt
objective: Use real project responses to adapt a delivery step, check its effect with others and preserve evidence of your leadership.

blocks.text: GROW · Art · Week 6. Trinity Arts Award Silver. Continue The Project And Adapt.
Objective: Use real project responses to adapt a delivery step, check its effect with others and preserve evidence of your leadership.
Success evidence: the genuine delivery phase, the reason for an agreed adjustment, your own action, others’ responses and a located before-and-after record.
Unit 2 is your arts leadership project. Keep it distinct from your personal arts challenge in Unit 1. These lessons support your real project at its planned scale.
40-minute lesson frame. Real activity may continue in recorded programme time. No event, attendance or booking is asserted here.

This deck directly serves Silver Unit 2, Arts leadership, Parts 2C and 2D. Part 2C requires effective arts leadership in actual delivery. Two delivery lessons may support phases of one project; they do not create a two-event minimum. Part 2D requires working effectively with others. Preserve the pupil’s own contribution, actual exchanges and response to collaborators. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Silver and universal rules. Silver has TWO units, evidenced separately: Unit 1 Arts practice and pathways; Unit 2 Arts leadership. Mark P / A / N per part. ONE Attempted is allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass / Below Pass only. The whole Silver portfolio has a 20-file cap across both units, not twenty per unit. Organise evidence by unit and part. Nine cumulative part files or two clearly sectioned unit files are optional layouts. Name the actual file plus page, slide or timecode for each item. One real record may support two parts with clear locators; do not count duplicate copies as extra evidence. The four assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, planning and review, and communication. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. Confirm these locally, not as an accomplished fact in this deck. Adults may scribe exact pupil words or confirmed signs and check them back, but must not write the pupil’s plan, review or evidence. Staff may separately record factual observations. Core, Extend and Challenge are support choices within Silver and retain the actual role, contribution and evidence. No public showing is imposed as a Silver requirement. Fourteen forty-minute sessions do not supply all 95 programme hours; record actual further guided and independent time.

Retrieve the pupil’s current role, delivery records and actual remaining project tasks. Use this lesson for needed delivery within the same project, not a required second workshop or event. If delivery is already complete, retain its existing evidence; review or rehearsal must not be relabelled as fresh delivery. Identify any genuine remaining phase with the pupil and responsible staff. Prepare current project materials and a safe place for small trials. For the classroom model, use a short pencil-mark instruction written small and then clearly on two paper cards. Label the model as a demonstration and use the willing partner’s real responses. Preserve original records before updates. Any change affecting risk, access, permission or a person’s role needs the relevant agreement before use.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Confirm actual remaining delivery. Never create a two-event requirement or present completed-project reflection as new delivery.

blocks.text: Open the delivery record. Find your role and an actual participant response. What does it show?
Check the remaining agreed work with the real plan and people.
If delivery is complete, keep its evidence. Ask staff about any needed follow-through; label reviews and rehearsals honestly.
Notice, check, adapt and look again. Changes should help the arts purpose and participants.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Label the case as a hypothetical teaching example. Invite several plausible interpretations without diagnosing or blaming a participant.

blocks.text: Consider this teaching case: a person keeps asking where to begin the art task. A leader decides that the whole group needs a harder task instead.
What evidence supports that decision? The question may show that the first step is unclear. It does not prove that the task is too easy.
An observation says what happened. An interpretation is what you think it might mean. Keep them separate until you check with the person involved.

Ask a question such as, Which part do you need to see again? A useful adjustment might be a clearer demonstration, a different position or more time. It might also be no change if you have misunderstood the issue.
Start from the real response. You do not need to invent a problem to show leadership.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Use real paper cards and a willing partner. Do not script the partner’s answer. Explain the purpose of keeping one variable steady in this practical trial.

blocks.text: Watch the adult test an explanation with a willing partner. The card says, Choose a mark and repeat it across the paper. First the writing is small and the card is placed at a distance.
The adult asks what the partner can see and what they need. They use the actual reply. If the writing is clear already, they say so; they do not manufacture a difficulty.

Now they show a larger-lettered version at the same position. The partner stays in the same viewing seat. Which version gives a clearer starting point? The partner’s actual answer supplies the comparison evidence.
The adult changes only the letter size in this trial. The wording, art task, card position and viewing seat stay the same. This makes it easier to judge whether the letter-size change helped.
They check the effect by inviting the partner to point to the first action or begin the marks. A yes alone may not show whether the next step is understood.
The adult records what was tried, the real response and the decision. If neither version helps, they keep that result and test another explanation. An unsuccessful trial can guide a useful next step.

blocks.title: Adapt from evidence during delivery
blocks.caption: A change is tested, not assumed to help.
blocks.alt: Adapt from evidence during delivery. NOTICE what really happened. CHECK ask what it means. ADAPT agree one safe change. LOOK AGAIN check the actual effect. A change is tested, not assumed to help.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Read the actual prompt and choices; support the pupil to commit before checking. Use the item feedback as a model reason, not a judgement on personal taste. Keep real trials, meetings, views and project actions separate from these teaching examples.

data.heading: Choose a respectful check before adapting
data.instruction: Everyone commits before we compare. Choose what the observation supports, then plan a check within your agreed role.

items.label: A participant pauses after the tool moves. What do you know?
items.feedback: The pause is observable. Its meaning needs a respectful check rather than a guess about the person.

options.label: They paused; I can ask which step or support they need.

items.label: Someone asks to see the first fold again. Which response leaves the making choice with them?
items.feedback: Show the requested action and check their real response. Repeating a step is not permission to finish their work.

options.label: Show that fold on scrap and invite them to try.
Fold their whole piece before they can respond.

items.label: The team checks the current method and finds it works for this phase. Must the leader change it?
items.feedback: Keeping a method for an evidence-based reason is a valid decision. Record the check and any remaining limits.

options.label: Yes; every comment must lead to a visible change.
No; keep it for a reason and record the actual check.

data.discussion: Use a real project response. Agree any change with the responsible people, keep the earlier state and check the effect with others.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Use the actual model cards as before-and-after evidence. Model permission boundaries without introducing additional qualification quotas.

blocks.text: Check who can agree the change. Moving a card may be within your role; a new room or tool may need further checks.
Discuss effects on resources, risk, access, timing and other people’s jobs with those responsible.
Keep original and updated states. Record the reason and result instead of hiding earlier difficulties.
For 2C, locate the leadership decision in real delivery. For 2D, show listening, agreement and shared action.
You may keep the current method. Record the evidence for that decision; leadership does not require a change after every comment.

blocks.title: A safe adjustment and an unsupported leap
blocks.caption: Keep the reason, agreement and real effect together.
blocks.alt: A safe adjustment and an unsupported leap. SUPPORTED CHANGE real response checked action agreed and tested. UNSUPPORTED LEAP a guess treated as fact new action without checks. Keep the reason, agreement and real effect together.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Help pupils select a manageable, genuine issue. Any unsafe resource is removed from use and referred to the responsible adult, not repeatedly tested.

blocks.text: Choose a small explanation or resource from your real project that could use a check. Keep the original version. Ask a collaborator to try it or review it from the position it will be used.
Listen to the actual response. Agree one safe adjustment to trial, or a reason to keep the method. Do not force a complaint when the step works.
Try the adjustment with suitable spare materials before changing the main activity. Check the result with the person who raised the issue. They may still need something different.
This lab is a practical trial. Label it as rehearsal unless it genuinely takes place within the agreed project delivery. Keep the distinction clear even when the same people are involved.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Preserve genuine delivery evidence rather than rewarding invented extra activity. Every route keeps pupil role, collaboration and accurate records; use extended programme time when needed.

blocks.text: Continue the real delivery phase that remains in your plan. Use your agreed role to support its arts purpose. Notice what people actually do, ask or show while taking part.
When a response calls for adjustment, check its meaning. Agree a safe change with the relevant people, try it and look for its effect. Keep enough of the earlier state to explain what changed.
Core: use a cue strip and access support while carrying out your own real delivery role. Check a response with a collaborator, contribute to the decision and record your action and the actual result.
Extend: lead your phase, make or retain a method for a reason and check the effect with others. Keep the original state, your decision and the true response.
Challenge: retain the same real delivery and collaboration evidence. Compare possible adjustments, explain the choice within your role and check whether it helped the intended arts outcome.

If no further delivery is needed, work from the actual existing evidence and label any review or preparation as such. Do not stage a pretend second session. Name any genuine delivery gap for staff to arrange.
Save the record under Unit 2, Parts 2C and 2D, with the actual file name and page, slide or timecode. Keep the pupil account separate from an observer’s factual note and from another person’s words.

stages.title: Exit · check the effect
stages.data-ta1: Check evidence and any remaining action. Do not require a positive result where the real trial showed otherwise.

blocks.text: Point to the response you checked and the decision that followed. What evidence shows the effect? It is acceptable to say that the result is still unclear or the change did not help.
Confirm the record with the people involved where needed. Make it clear who suggested the change, who agreed it and what you personally did. Shared work does not mean everyone did the same thing.

Keep unfinished practical matters visible for the team. Save the precise location of the record so you can use it in your later review. A truthful limit is more useful than a success claim with nothing behind it.

print.intro: Use actual project responses to make an agreed safe adjustment. Keep its real effect and your own role; no extra event is required.
focusRows: What happened in the real phase, and what did I check?
What was agreed, by whom, and what did I personally do?
What before-and-after evidence shows the effect or its limits?
tiers: Core: use a cue strip and access support while carrying out your own real delivery role. Check a response with a collaborator, contribute to the decision and record your action and the actual result.
Extend: lead your phase, make or retain a method for a reason and check the effect with others. Keep the original state, your decision and the true response.
Challenge: retain the same real delivery and collaboration evidence. Compare possible adjustments, explain the choice within your role and check whether it helped the intended arts outcome.
checks: Actual delivery is identified; review or rehearsal is not falsely counted as a new event.
The adjustment or decision to retain a method follows a checked response.
Risk, access and other people’s roles were considered before a change.
My own leadership and work with others remain identifiable, including an unclear or unsuccessful result.
Unit 2 Parts 2C and 2D have actual file-plus-page, slide or timecode locators.
